I used to contract out for a loan company dealing with reclaiming houses. I worked in a very progressive state so if it was this easy here I imagine it's easier most places. First they wouldn't even begin the eviction process for a long time. YOu'd have to skip like a year of payments. (not this is all for mortgaged properties not rentals) The court would authorize the eviction. I'd get a piece of paper with all the legal details and the eviction date(about a month out). You go to the property and serve the person the paper. If they aren't there you tape it to the door which counts as them being served. You drive by a couple time during the month to see if they have left. 90 % of the people would voluntarily leave once they had been served.

If they are still there on the eviction day, you call the police. A sheriff shows up. The go to the door and tell the person they have to get out and remove all personal belongings. If they continue to not leave, the sheriff calls in backup. A group of deputies would show up with garbage bags. They would remove the people to public property and tell them they can't set a foot on the reclaimed property or they would be arrested for trespassing. One deputy would watch the people while the rest went into the property and removed all personal items. They were also placed on the public property. All but one of the deputies would leave. Usually the new guy would have to wait there making sure the people didn't interfere as we changed the locks. Then everybody leaves

The sheriff and deputies were usually really nice to the people. Would not evict if the weather was bad.

In the 2 years I did it part time I only witnessed one bad incident and yes it involved a fat. She attacked the sheriff with a broom. Pro LIfe tip.. don't attack cops.
